transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As part of our normal pre-settlement control meeting, I need to sign off on a collateral substitution. We want to replace part of the government bonds currently pledged under the central-bank liquidity facility with investment-grade corporate bonds, so we can free up some government bonds to support an upcoming client settlement. To recap the key figures: we have $6 million outstanding under the facility, $10 million in government bonds pledged, and the facility requires collateral valued at least 1.25 times the outstanding borrowing. Before I make my decision, I'd like each of you to report any relevant requirements or concerns from your areas. Collateral risk, let's start with you — what do we need to watch on the corporate bonds from a collateral valuation and eligibility standpoint?

Thank you all for those important inputs. Let me summarize what I'm hearing and identify the gaps before I can decide.

From collateral risk (Elias): We have a qualifying corporate-bond basket with $9,400,000 market value and a 20% haircut. That means the collateral value after haircut would be $7,520,000. The basket analysis still needs to be uploaded to the facility file.

From legal (Nadia): Two requirements — a 30% max single-issuer exposure limit on substituted corporate bonds, and a signed collateral-amendment acknowledgment must be in place before settlement.

From relationship coverage (Leila): The client settlement requires exactly $9,000,000 of government bonds released on 2026-08-19, but this isn't yet in the operational systems.

From treasury operations (Victor): I didn't catch your input clearly — could you repeat your requirements or concerns?

Now, let me work through the math. We have $6,000,000 outstanding, and the facility requires collateral valued at 1.25x that, so $7,500,000 minimum collateral value after haircuts. If we release $9,000,000 of government bonds, we'd have $1,000,000 of government bonds remaining (with no haircut, so $1,000,000 collateral value) plus the corporate basket at $7,520,000 after the 20% haircut, totaling $8,520,000. That exceeds the $7,500,000 requirement — so on the surface the substitution appears feasible.

However, before I can sign off, I need: (1) confirmation from Victor on treasury operations requirements, (2) confirmation that the corporate basket complies with the 30% single-issuer limit, (3) the basket analysis uploaded to the facility file, (4) the collateral-amendment acknowledgment signed, and (5) the $9,000,000 release instruction visible in operational systems. Victor, could you please restate your points?
